purpose: library: protein synthesis as an ordered two-step process — transcription (the information in a gene's DNA passed to messenger RNA in the cell nucleus; RNA and DNA both nucleotide chains with slightly different chemical properties; mRNA carrying the message to the cytoplasm) and translation (the ribosome reading the mRNA nucleotide sequence; each three-nucleotide codon usually coding one amino acid; transfer RNA assembling the protein one amino acid at a time until a stop codon), together called gene expression — the DNA→RNA→protein flow known as the central dogma. Fits step ordering of transcription→translation, quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on codon length and the stop signal, and a concept map of DNA/mRNA/ribosome/tRNA roles. The page carries a labelled central-dogma figure (not stored; a future diagram engine could use the real page image).
